gap: No result ChatGPT got states that USB-C-to-USB-C fast charging (140 W) of a 16-inch MacBook Pro only works on the Nov 2023 model and later; Apple lists Apple's USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable as the only fast-charge route for older 16-inch models. MacRumors reports the 2021/2022 16-inch models are capped at 100 W over USB-C, and ChargerLAB measured an M1 Max 16-inch at 89.88 W over USB-C versus 130.02 W over MagSafe 3. So a 140 W bank's built-in USB-C cable cannot fast-charge those older 16-inch machines.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld (cited, 2026-11-04). It says the 16-inch Pro needs a 140 W PD 3.1 bank, and that the Anker Prime 26K can fast-charge it with Apple's USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable or the included 240 W cable. It gives no model-year limit, so the 240 W USB-C route reads as working on every 16-inch Pro. Its suited-to lists mark 140 W built-in-cable banks (Reelcharge, EcoFlow) as suiting the '14/16" MBP' without any year caveat. Macworld names no 5 A/EPR/e-marker rule beyond that one 240 W mention. The cited Wirecutter page could not be read (the proxy now returns a refusal message), and the ChatGPT answer itself has no cable or model-year caveat.
decides: For a 16-inch MacBook Pro from Nov 2023 or later, any 140 W port bank (UGREEN 145W, Anker Prime 26K) works with a 240 W / 5 A USB-C cable. For a 2021 to early-2023 16-inch Pro, the pick must be a bank with a free USB-C port that reaches 140 W, used with Apple's USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable. Built-in-cable banks (Anker A1695, capped at 100 W on every cable; the Baseus FC41's built-in cables) then charge at about 100 W at best. For a 14-inch Pro or MacBook Air, Apple lists 96 W (or 67 W for the 13.6-inch Air) over plain USB-C as fast charge, so the 100 W Anker A1695 is enough and 140 W adds nothing.

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro fast-charge combinations listed by Apple
findings.value: '140W USB-C Power Adapter + USB-C to MagSafe 3 Cable' (16-inch, 2021 or later); '140W USB-C Power Adapter + 240W USB-C Charge Cable for MacBook Pro (16-inch, Nov 2023) or later'
findings.source_title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: The USB-C cable route is limited to 16-inch Nov 2023 and later. Apple names only its own 140 W adapter and gives no guidance on third-party adapters or power banks.

findings.label: 14-inch MacBook Pro and MacBook Air fast-charge combinations listed by Apple
findings.value: 14-inch Pro (2021+): 96 W or 140 W adapter with USB-C to MagSafe 3 or USB-C charge cable. MacBook Air (2022+): 70 W, 96 W or 140 W, plus 67 W for 13.6-inch models only, with either cable
findings.source_title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: A plain USB-C cable is fine for these models. A 100 W bank exceeds the 96 W listed for the 14-inch Pro.

findings.label: USB-C ceiling on 2021/2022 16-inch MacBook Pro
findings.value: 100 W over USB-C; 140 W only via Apple's USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable
findings.source_title: 16-Inch M3 MacBook Pro Can Fast Charge Over USB-C With 240W Cable (Juli Clover, MacRumors, 2023-11-07)
findings.note: Quote: '2021 and 2022 16-inch MacBook Pro models with M-series chips are limited to faster 140W charging with the USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable ... with the USB-C ports offering only up to 100W.' The same article says M3 16-inch models fast charge at 140 W over USB-C with a 240 W cable.

findings.label: Measured draw of a 16-inch M1 Max MacBook Pro, MagSafe 3 vs USB-C
findings.value: 130.02 W (27.66 V × 4.7 A) via MagSafe 3; 89.88 W (19.37 V × 4.64 A) via USB-C to USB-C
findings.source_title: Charging Review of Movespeed 140W PD3.1 4-in-1 Charger (ChargerLAB, 2024-06-30)
findings.note: ChargerLAB measured this on a Movespeed 140 W wall charger, not a power bank. The same laptop drew 40 W more on the MagSafe 3 cable.

findings.label: Apple's rule for non-Apple USB-C power sources
findings.value: Any USB PD adapter works, even at lower wattage than recommended. Recommended adapter for the 16-inch MacBook Pro (2021+) is the 140 W adapter with USB-C to MagSafe 3
findings.source_title: Use a power adapter with your Mac - Apple Support
findings.note: This page does not mention a 240 W cable.

findings.label: Port outputs and cable requirement stated by Anker
findings.value: USB-C up to 140 W (top step 28 V⎓5 A); USB-A 22.5 W; 300 W total. '140W input with a compatible 140W charger and a 5A cable'
findings.note: The page lists MacBook Air/Pro, Dell XPS, ThinkPad, Surface and Galaxy Book as compatible, with no exclusions. It does not state what cable is in the box (Macworld says a 240 W cable). Price $229.99 on anker.com.

findings.label: Per-cable/port ceiling stated by Anker
findings.value: Every USB-C cable and port up to 20 V⎓5 A (100 W max); USB-A 33 W; 165 W total across two USB-C; 130 W total with 3–4 devices
findings.source_title: Anker Power Bank (25K, 165W, Built-In and Retractable Cables)
findings.note: No output reaches 140 W, so it cannot fast-charge any 16-inch MacBook Pro per Apple's list. 100 W does exceed the 96 W Apple lists for the 14-inch Pro. Anker lists 'MacBook Air/Pro series' as compatible, and its only stated exclusion is that Lightning iPhones need an adapter (not included). Price $119.99 on anker.com.

unsourced: UGREEN 145W 25000mAh (ugreen.com/products/usa-90597a): which port gives 140 W, the multi-port split, and whether a 240 W cable is in the box. The UGREEN store returned HTTP 429 three times (WebFetch and storecheck). storecheck search also returned $1300.00 for every UGREEN listing, which looks like a tool error, so I took no price from it.

Baseus EnerFill FC41: which output (built-in cable vs USB-C port) reaches 140 W, plus the per-port split. baseus.com returned 429 twice; the manuals.plus copy and the Notebookcheck launch article returned 403. Retailer listings found by search conflict (100 W vs 140 W USB-C).
Wirecutter's cited power-bank page: the proxy URL ChatGPT used now returns a refusal message instead of the article.
Windows laptops (Dell XPS, ThinkPad, Surface) that take only 100 W PD 3.0 rather than 140 W EPR from a PD 3.1 bank: I did not reach a maker document within the call budget.
A named reviewer's measurement of a Nov 2023+ 16-inch MacBook Pro charging from one of these power banks over a 240 W USB-C cable.
